Dev delivery is verified by successful pipeline executions, including release `7c97ec40-371c-4387-8c26-817c75450d4c` (data, migration, app, web, frontend sync and smoke). slices.S1: Enabled dev release 7969a830-cd94-41da-bf97-6693b389e17d succeeded with backend #29 and merged frontend #22. Both native browser cases pass in pipeline smoke; repeated seed creates/renews nothing. Real Google owner sign-in/repeat/logout/reload and unchanged persisted binding counts are verified. A separate real uninvited Google account is refused and remains absent from Cognito. S1-13 is complete. The owner reports the deactivated-account slice demo passed on dev with a second real Google account (2026-10-13). Cold-start evidence from the existing dev logs is recorded in ADR-0007 and accepted by the owner; it is not an on-demand p99. Future role-specific navigation acceptance (S1-11) remains open. The owner retains the sole dev admin; prod auth/deploy remain disabled.

S1-01.notes: Dev pool, Google provider, SPA and test client pass resource checks. Backend #28 is merged and released in 11d38ada-a392-471f-bf45-81592cedf9a5; live trigger alias is version 4. Owner reported successful real Google sign-in, and browser verification confirms admin profile, repeat sign-in after hosted logout and reload reauthentication. Prod remains disabled.

S1-02.notes: Owner accepted ADR-0008–0011 on 2026-10-11; decisions are merged in all three repositories. Live binding and latency proof are separate S1-18 acceptance work.

S1-03.notes: The merged trigger admits the real invited Google owner and refuses a separate real uninvited Google account with SIGN_UP_NOT_ALLOWED on version 5; Cognito identity count remains zero after refusal. PostgreSQL and privacy tests cover expired/accepted invitations and deactivated users. The read-only role and warmed alias are deployed. The owner reports the returning-deactivated-account slice demo passed on dev with a second real Google account (2026-10-13); no account identifier or screenshot is committed. Latency: the owner accepted the existing dev CloudWatch evidence recorded in ADR-0007 (32 environment init durations, max 3.06 s; 7 first invocations, max 1.47 s; 113 warm invocations, p99 71.8 ms). That is not an on-demand cold-start p99: the sample is small, the logs cannot show true cold starts because reserved and provisioned concurrency are both 1, and headroom under the 5 s ceiling is about 0.5 s.

S1-04.notes: Identity migration and sqlc lookups are merged and applied on dev; PostgreSQL lifecycle, uniqueness and idempotency tests pass.

S1-05.notes: The /me contract and shared auth Problem responses are merged and released with frontend S1-19. The real /me endpoint remains S1-08.

S1-15.notes: Trusted authorizer claims are carried through the Lambda adapter and released to dev. Protected-route integration remains S1-06/S1-14.

S1-17.notes: presignup_ro bootstrap and exact SELECT grants on users/invitations are merged and deployed. Negative privilege tests cover writes and unrelated future tables; the deployed trigger uses its scoped IAM connection.

S1-19.notes: Frontend /me spec, generated types and test handler are merged and released with backend S1-05. The API drift gate and frontend tests pass; real endpoint/auth UI work remains S1-08/S1-10.

S1-09.notes: Seed/admin invitation and all three confirmed native fixtures are deployed. Successful repeat enabled release 11d38ada-a392-471f-bf45-81592cedf9a5 reports accounts_created=0, invitations_created=0, invitations_renewed=0 and synthetic_users_created=0. Owner Google admin sign-in succeeds. Recovery implementation is merged; owner retains the sole real dev admin.

S1-06.notes: Merged identity middleware is deployed. Real Google owner sign-in and repeat sign-in resolve the admin profile; read-only operator checks before/after the repeat confirm one Google identity, one matching active admin user/subject and one accepted invitation. Native Gateway invited/uninvited acceptance and PostgreSQL transactional/concurrency/role/deactivation regressions pass.

S1-07.notes: Backend #24 is merged and released. Central active-actor, same-org self/admin/supervisor/peer policies deny by default, require accepted relationships and reject storage errors. Admin grants no supervision override. /me demonstrates the handler policy call; later slices implement relationship storage.

S1-08.notes: The deployed /me endpoint resolves the real Google owner and displays Default Organization and the database admin role. Repeat sign-in and reload resolve the profile again. Native tests verify invited 200 and uninvited 403, explicit DTO and no-store handling.

S1-14.notes: Dev activation 248fa024-49a0-4ebc-bc76-73a236ca9aaa succeeded after the official-registry repair. Live Gateway/native smoke passes invited /me 200, uninvited 403, authenticated unknown 404 and unauthenticated 401; health remains public. Exactly one public route, issuer/audiences and scoped reader are asserted. Backend #28 subsequently released in 11d38ada-a392-471f-bf45-81592cedf9a5; real Google owner profile acceptance also passes.

S1-16.notes: Released in successful enabled-dev activation 248fa024-49a0-4ebc-bc76-73a236ca9aaa. Exact Cognito CSP and no-store public issuer/client/callback/logout settings are verified, with no credential fields. Release header/browser checks and native dev browser flows pass. Prod remains disabled.

S1-10.notes: Frontend #21 is merged and deployed. Actual Google admin sign-in, hosted logout to the signed-out landing, repeat sign-in and page-reload reauthentication were observed on dev after backend #28. Memory-only tokens, state/nonce/PKCE, callback cleanup, refresh/revocation and error handling have automated coverage. Native runner refresh-token revocation is verified separately; no real owner credential was recorded.

S1-11.notes: Deployed landing, admin profile, account menu and signed-out view were verified with the real owner Google account. Native denial and accessibility cases pass. Navigation for future role-specific feature pages remains pending with those features.

S1-12.notes: Backend #25 is merged at 8e1e29210edbe033646560d5f3523cb2ad669513 and released successfully in 79a1a47a-bc74-4a3a-be9b-923511bfc5f5. PostgreSQL regressions prove unchanged trusted claims cannot retain removed database roles or bypass deactivation; the runbook documents next-request enforcement and S5-05 Cognito follow-up. Real native/Google profile acceptance is verified separately. No live owner demotion or deactivation was performed.

S1-20.notes: Backend #26 and infra #38 are merged. PostgreSQL recovery tests preserve the first bound admin/history, are idempotent and require explicit prod opt-in. The runbook gives exact additional-admin invocation and safe failure handling. Owner explicitly elected to retain the sole dev admin; no second live identity or live recovery drill is claimed.

S1-13.notes: Frontend #22 is merged and released. Both native invited/denied browser cases explicitly passed in pipeline smoke in d41c4fb4-4e96-42d8-98bc-67da2a878869 and 7969a830-cd94-41da-bf97-6693b389e17d. The separate real Google demo records owner sign-in/repeat/logout/reload and uninvited denial; the uninvited account has zero Cognito identities before and after. No real credentials or identities were committed; automated tests do not drive Google. The owner reports the deactivated-account slice demo passed separately on dev with a second real Google account (2026-10-13).

S1-18.notes: Backend #29 is merged and released successfully in 7969a830-cd94-41da-bf97-6693b389e17d. Read-only owner verification before and after another real Google sign-in returns one Google identity and unchanged counts of one user, subject match, active admin and accepted invitation. Real uninvited Google sign-in is refused with SIGN_UP_NOT_ALLOWED (handler duration 69 ms, version 5) and creates no Cognito identity. Backend #33 records the existing dev CloudWatch cold-start evidence in ADR-0007, accepted by the owner in place of a probe run: it states that no p99 is claimed, that the logs cannot show on-demand cold starts, and that headroom under the 5 s ceiling is about 0.5 s. No AWS resource was changed. ADR-0008 records binding proof; production and the sole-admin decision are unchanged.
